title: Design Jev code-health checks as a shadow-mode design doc
summary: Write docs/design/jev-code-health.md (no code): typed Jev questions for judging changed files and functions, each with state, options, criteria, threshold and effect, run in shadow mode and scored by later evidence, plus fit with deterministic code-health, Hestia and the scope guard, and cost per landing. Add a proposed decision entry and a build plan of one-producer-run jobs. Audience: Sri, who will judge whether the checks are specified well enough to build.

defaults_applied.how: Doc gives alternatives considered (e.g. line-count only, model per file vs per function) and a proposed decision for review before any build.
Costs and call counts are measured from cited docs or labeled as estimates; scoring evidence is defined from landing records.
Scoring criteria name observable later events (flagged file breaks or churns; recommended split lands and churn drops), not wiring.
Build plan split into jobs each sized for one producer run.
Doc written for an outside reader, defining Jev and the shadow period.
Each question's effect and the shadow-period exit rule are tied to measured outcomes.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Jev's calling convention is read from docs/design/defaults-loop.md section 6 and cited, not restated from memory.
The deterministic code-health check of request 20261026-042558-5p65 is not yet built; the doc refers to it as planned, with its measures and thresholds as that request states them.
docs/design/hestia.md exists (from 20261025-033743-npr5) and docs/design/scope-guard.md exists; the doc cites both rather than changing them.
Costs are computed from the stated $0.00001 per call times a stated calls-per-landing count, labeled as estimates.
Questions proposed: function-does-one-thing, adds-coupling, which-module-for-new-item, god-object-drift, duplicates-existing-logic.
The decisions.md entry is marked proposed, not accepted; build plan items are listed in the design doc and in the decisions entry.
No code, athena.toml or workflow changes; shadow mode needs only a records format that the build plan describes.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/jev-code-health.md has, for each of at least five questions (one-thing-or-several, added coupling, module placement, god-object drift, duplicated logic), the state given to Jev (bounded excerpt and context), the options, the criteria, a numeric confidence threshold, and the effect of a confident answer (status finding, structural-pass request via 20261026-042558-5p65, or nothing).

The doc defines the shadow period (answers recorded, no action), its exit rule, and the evidence that scores each question: a flagged file that later breaks or churns, and a recommended split that lands and reduces churn, with how each is measured from landing records.

The doc explains how the checks relate to the deterministic code-health measures, Hestia and the scope guard, citing those docs, and gives cost per landing as calls times $0.00001 with the call-count assumption labeled as an estimate.

docs/decisions.md gains one entry marked proposed (not accepted) with alternatives, and the doc's build plan lists jobs each stated as sized for one producer run with files and a test or demonstration per job.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the design; no files outside docs/design/jev-code-health.md, docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md change, and cargo test still passes (any doc/decision link test is satisfied).
Run cargo test from the repository root: all tests pass, including any test that checks decisions.md format or links.

out_of_scope: Implementing any Jev call, question runner or status display
Building the deterministic code-health check of 20261026-042558-5p65
Changing Hestia, scope guard, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
urgent_reason: Without these checks, files grow into god objects unnoticed and cost failed or rejected attempts, thrash and redo-work retries; designing them now cuts that wasted time.
